items.q: Why ask for an outline before prose?
options: Structure is cheap to change; finished prose invites wording edits instead of structural ones
Prose consumes more of a usage allowance
items.explain: Once text reads well you tighten sentences rather than asking whether a section should exist — sunk cost on something that cost you nothing.

items.q: An outline section should state:
items.explain: "Background" tells you nothing. A claim can be agreed with, disagreed with, or evidenced.

items.q: Requesting an outline on a subject you know nothing about produces:
options: A reliable structure drawn from wide reading
A plausible-shaped outline reflecting convention rather than your situation
items.explain: It mirrors how such documents usually look. Useful as a prompt for your own thinking, not as an answer.

items.q: The strongest reason to draft one section at a time:
options: A gap in your argument gets bridged with confident prose when the whole thing is written at once
items.explain: Fluent connective writing hides weak transitions. Section by section, the gap stays visible.

items.q: The best way to specify your writing voice:
options: Paste 300–500 words of your own typical writing
items.explain: Adjectives select an average. Your own typical writing is evidence the model can match.

items.q: Keeping a list of your assistant's verbal tells lets you:
options: Forbid specific habits by name rather than asking for 'natural' writing
Detect when the model has been updated
items.explain: A named habit is a concrete instruction; "sound human" is another adjective to interpret.

items.q: Critiquing writing you have already done is safer than drafting because:
options: You know the material, so verification costs almost nothing
items.explain: You can judge each objection instantly — the ideal case from E4·L1.

items.q: Why forbid the assistant from saying what works in a critique?
options: Balancing criticism with reassurance dilutes the part you needed
items.explain: Left open, a model softens criticism with encouragement. You asked for objections.

items.q: "Where will a reader misunderstand this?" is valuable because:
options: It is a question you structurally cannot answer about your own writing
Models are trained on reader feedback
items.explain: You read your own meaning into your sentences. A system producing the most likely reading is the approximation you need.

items.q: When a critique lands, you should:
options: Take the objection and rewrite it yourself
items.explain: Rewriting is where your judgement and understanding are built. Hand it back and the artefact improves while you do not.

items.q: The most valuable element of a spreadsheet formula request:
options: Sample rows plus the expected answers for them
items.explain: Stating expected answers gives the request a right answer and surfaces a misunderstanding before you build on it.

items.q: Which test most reliably catches a broken formula?
options: Running it on rows where you already know the answer
Asking whether the assistant is confident
items.explain: Known-answer rows, plus an empty one and an odd one, take about thirty seconds. Stated confidence is not evidence.

items.q: Spreadsheet errors are especially dangerous because:
options: A wrong formula returns a plausible number silently and is then copied down
items.explain: Wrong prose usually reads oddly; a wrong number looks exactly like a right one, and propagates.

items.q: Why should you always ask a formula to explain itself?
options: Reading it is how you notice an assumption you did not intend
It is required by most spreadsheet applications
items.explain: "This treats blanks as zero" is how you catch a mismatch with what you needed — and it makes the sheet maintainable later.

items.q: A total produced in prose is unreliable because:
options: It is generated as likely text rather than computed
items.explain: The model produces text fitting the pattern of a total. Nothing in the prose distinguishes a correct one from a near-miss.

items.q: The safe division of labour with data:
options: Assistant for the method, spreadsheet for the arithmetic
Spreadsheet for the method, assistant for the arithmetic
items.explain: It keeps the model where it is strong and keeps computation reproducible and traceable to a cell someone can open.

items.q: A percentage change quoted without a stated base is:
options: Acceptable if the direction is right
Not a fact — the base determines what it means
Fine in summaries but not reports
items.explain: Against last month, last year, or budget are different claims, and a model will pick a plausible base without telling you.

items.q: Asking for 'a deck about X' produces weak slides because:
options: A topic has no order or claim, and a presentation is an argument in sequence
items.explain: Topics yield parallel bullets that assert nothing. The argument has to exist before any slide does.

items.q: An assertion headline is:
options: A title stating the slide's claim as a full sentence
The first bullet promoted to the title
items.explain: A claim is arguable and checkable, and a reader skimming only your titles still receives the whole argument.

items.q: A slide requiring two separate pieces of evidence should be:
options: Reduced to one piece with the other in a footnote
items.explain: Two pieces of evidence means two claims are hiding in one slide.

items.q: A good rewrite for a different audience changes:
options: What is included and the order it appears in
items.explain: Vocabulary was rarely the barrier. Different readers need different content, led by what they must decide.

items.q: The main risk when simplifying a document:
options: A caveat is dropped, so the simpler version claims more than the evidence supports
items.explain: Qualifiers sound least essential and go first — and the remaining sentence is one you will be held to.

items.q: Drafting a document section by section predictably introduces:
options: Assembly errors — inconsistent terms, repeated points, conflicting figures
items.explain: Individually fine sections that do not quite agree. That is exactly what a mechanical pass is good at finding.

items.q: Which final check has no mechanical version?
options: Whether the document is fair to the people named in it
items.explain: Consistency and arithmetic can be checked. Whether someone would recognise themselves, and whether you would say it with them present, cannot.
